headline: Rabindranath Tagore mural defaced with black ink in Khulna
summary: The artwork, located on the boundary wall of Khulna Railway Station, was targeted by miscreants, sparking widespread condemnation.
details: Miscreants have defaced a mural of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore with black ink on the boundary wall of Khulna Railway Station. The incident was discovered on Friday morning.

The murals were commissioned by the Khulna City Corporation (KCC) and feature portraits of eminent figures such as Tagore, Kazi Nazrul Islam, and SM Sultan, alongside depictions of the July Uprising and the Sundarbans.
Of all the portraits on the wall, only Tagore's portrait was targeted and defaced with black ink, leaving other figures like Kazi Nazrul Islam and Fakir Lalon Shah untouched.
Cultural activist Shariful Islam Salim described the incident as the work of an organised group, noting that similar acts have occurred in Dhaka.
Salim emphasized that Tagore's philosophy of secularism and human dignity continues to inspire generations and called for the unity of people against such acts.
Khulna Sadar Police Station officer-in-charge Lokman Hossain stated that the perpetrators have not yet been identified, but police are currently investigating the matter.

Cultural activist Shariful Islam Salim described the incident as the work of an organised group, noting that similar acts have occurred in Dhaka.

Salim emphasized that Tagore's philosophy of secularism and human dignity continues to inspire generations and called for the unity of people against such acts.

headline: BJP MP calls for reclaiming Noakhali, Chittagong Port, and Sylhet from Bangladesh
summary: Lawmaker Nishikant Dubey claims these territories were handed over to East Pakistan during Partition without the consent of the Tripura kingdom's ruler.
details: Indian BJP lawmaker Nishikant Dubey has called for India to "reclaim" Noakhali, Chittagong Port, and Sylhet from Bangladesh, according to reports from The Hindu and ANI.

Dubey alleged that India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, forcibly handed over these regions to East Pakistan during the 1947 Partition to secure the Muslim League's support in the interim government.
The lawmaker claimed that Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya, the then king of Tripura, had opposed the decision and challenged Nehru over the handover of these territories.
The remarks received backing from Pradyot Manikya, head of the Tipra Motha party and a descendant of the royal family of Tripura.
Pradyot Manikya argued that the loss of Chattogram would have provided northeastern India with direct sea access, removing the dependency on the narrow 'Chicken's Neck' corridor.
Dubey stated that just as India seeks to reclaim Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, it is now time to reclaim these territories from Bangladesh.
caption:
A BJP lawmaker is calling for India to 'reclaim' Noakhali, Chittagong Port, and Sylhet from Bangladesh.

Indian BJP lawmaker Nishikant Dubey has called for India to "reclaim" Noakhali, Chittagong Port, and Sylhet from Bangladesh, according to reports from The Hindu and ANI.

Dubey alleged that India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, forcibly handed over these regions to East Pakistan during the 1947 Partition to secure the Muslim League's support in the interim government.

The lawmaker claimed that Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya, the then king of Tripura, had opposed the decision and challenged Nehru over the handover of these territories.

The remarks received backing from Pradyot Manikya, head of the Tipra Motha party and a descendant of the royal family of Tripura.

Pradyot Manikya argued that the loss of Chattogram would have provided northeastern India with direct sea access, removing the dependency on the narrow 'Chicken's Neck' corridor.

Dubey stated that just as India seeks to reclaim Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, it is now time to reclaim these territories from Bangladesh.
